newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus signs deal with French film producers.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus signs deal with French film producers.

text.p: French pay television group Canal Plus said it signed a new deal with French film producers -- in which it has no stake or only a small stake -- under which it would pre-purchase 75 percent of its first-run films from them.
It said in a statement over the weekend that the accord would come into force after a transition period of three years.
Canal Plus would still be able to use at least 30 percent of the funds allocated in 1997 to pre-purchase French films to producers affiliated with Canal Plus under the accord, it added.
The accord would allow Canal Plus to invest more in French films than it is legally obliged to do, it said.
The accord was signed with the Societe Civile des Auteurs Realisateurs et Producteurs (ARP) and the Bureau de Liaison des Industries Cinematographiques (BLIC).
Canal Plus has holdings of over 15 percent in two French film production houses, a Canal Plus spokeswoman said. The accord applies to film producers in which it holds less than 15 percent.
Up to now the French pay TV channel has had no special deal with independant film producers, she said.
